rationale:
The supplied proof has two different mathematical ingredients, so the split follows them. Each child is a genuine, reusable obligation.

(1) coarea_straightening_submersion_chart covers steps 3-5 and the identity Phi(Lambda p) = p from step 6(e). It is the Euclidean local submersion (rectification) theorem (cf. Spivak, Calculus on Manifolds, Thm 2-13): a C^1 map G on an open V in R^{m+k} with DG(a) surjective has a C^1 inverse chart Lambda : Omega -> V with G o Lambda = fst and DLambda bijective. It does not involve f or M and is the analytic core of the proof (inverse function theorem, openness of the invertibility set, derivative of the local inverse). The pinned Mathlib does not contain it: Geometry/Manifold/Submersion.lean defers "surjective derivative implies normal form" to future work, and Implicit.lean only gives the strict-derivative implicit partial homeomorphism onto F x ker f'.

(2) coarea_straightening_reparametrize_chart covers step 6 (a)-(d) and (f). Precomposing a Simon local representation psi that satisfies the tangent identity with such a C^1 diffeomorphism Lambda gives a C^1 injective immersion psi o Lambda with image O cap M for an open O (Simon 4.2). The composite still satisfies the tangent identity. It does not involve f.

How the children give the selected statement, following the supplied proof. The parent keeps steps 1-2: it picks a chart (V, W, psi) with x0 = psi(a), sets G := f o psi, which is C^1 on V because psi(V) is in M, which is in U, and shows DG(a) = Df(x0) o Dpsi(a) is surjective. Surjectivity comes from hT and part (1) of the parent's resolved dependency coarea_jacobian_linear_algebra. The parent then:
- applies child 1 to (V, G, a), giving Omega and Lambda;
- applies child 2 to (psi, hT V W psi, Omega, Lambda), giving O;
- takes Psi := psi o Lambda.
From child 2 it gets: Omega and O open, Psi C^1 and injective on Omega, Psi(Omega) = O cap M, DPsi(p) injective, and the tangent identity. Since a is in Lambda(Omega), x0 = psi(a) lies in Psi(Omega) = O cap M, so x0 is in O. Finally f(Psi p) = G(Lambda p) = WithLp.fst p by child 1.
The uncle dependency is used only in the parent. Neither child needs a non-sibling dependency, and the two children are independent of each other.

Machine checks (scratch /tmp/straight-decomp-cThsEp, pinned Lean v4.35.0-rc3 with the pinned mathlib and simongmt oleans):

- Complete proofs of both children compile, with #print axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Comparator-style `exact Submission.X` files compile with the same axioms.
- Assembly2.lean proves the selected frozen type from the real child proofs plus a sorried stand-in of the sibling's frozen type; both types are string-identical to dag.json, and the only sorry is that stand-in.
- Neither name appears in dag.json or anywhere in the run directory. The c1_sard level_set_chart and chart_composition nodes have different types, so nothing is reused.

Citations: Spivak Thm 2-13 statement and IFT-based proof as transcribed at https://www.physicsforums.com/threads/spivaks-proof-not-clear-theorem-2-13.1024298/ and https://www.scribd.com/document/381161720/Spivak (called the rectification theorem there); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_function_theorem.

subproblems.title: Local submersion (rectification) chart for a C¹ map ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᵐ with surjective derivative
subproblems.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^{m+k} (= Rn (m + k)) and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), the Euclidean product, with first-component map p ↦ WithLp.fst p. Let V ⊆ E be open, let G : E → ℝᵐ be of class C¹ on V, and let a ∈ V be such that the derivative fderiv ℝ G a : E → ℝᵐ is surjective. Then there are an open set Ω ⊆ P and a map Λ : P → E with the following properties: Λ is C¹ on Ω and injective on Ω; the image Λ(Ω) is open, contains a and is contained in V; for every p ∈ Ω the derivative fderiv ℝ Λ p : P → E is bijective; and G(Λ p) = WithLp.fst p for every p ∈ Ω.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m) (a : Rn (m + k)), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G V → a ∈ V → Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ G a) → ∃ (Ω : Set (WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k))) (Λ : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) → Rn (m + k)), IsOpen Ω ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Λ Ω ∧ InjOn Λ Ω ∧ IsOpen (Λ '' Ω) ∧ a ∈ Λ '' Ω ∧ Λ '' Ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ p ∈ Ω, Function.Bijective (fderiv ℝ Λ p)) ∧ ∀ p ∈ Ω, G (Λ p) = WithLp.fst p
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3-5 of the parent proof, together with the identity Φ(Λ p) = p from its step 6(e). This is the local submersion (rectification) theorem (cf. Spivak, Calculus on Manifolds, Thm 2-13), proved with the inverse function theorem.

Notation.
- E := Rn (m + k) = ℝ^{m+k}; P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ); for p ∈ P, p₁ := WithLp.fst p.
- T : ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ → P, T(u, w) := WithLp.toLp 2 (u, w). T is a continuous linear equivalence, namely (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ ℝᵐ ℝᵏ).symm, and WithLp.fst (T(u, w)) = u holds by definition.
- All spaces here are finite-dimensional, hence complete, and every linear map between them is continuous. dim E = m + k and dim P = dim(ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) = m + k.
No case distinction is needed: the argument is also valid when m = 0 or k = 0, where ℝ⁰ is the zero space.

1. Regularity of G. V is open and G is C¹ on V. So for every x ∈ V, G is differentiable at x with Fréchet derivative DG(x) := fderiv ℝ G x.
2. Kernel dimension. L := DG(a) is surjective, so range L = ℝᵐ has dimension m. By rank-nullity, dim range L + dim ker L = dim E = m + k. Hence K₀ := ker L has dimension k.
3. A linear map that is injective on K₀.
   - Since dim K₀ = k = dim ℝᵏ, there is a linear isomorphism e : K₀ → ℝᵏ (LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq).
   - The inclusion ι : K₀ → E is injective, so it has a linear left inverse r : E → K₀ with r(ι v) = v for all v ∈ K₀ (LinearMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injective; the orthogonal projection onto K₀ also works).
   - Put π := e ∘ r : E → ℝᵏ, a continuous linear map. Then π(v) = e(r(ι v)) = e(v) for every v ∈ K₀.
4. The completed map. Define Φ : E → P by Φ(x) := T(G(x), π(x − a)). Then WithLp.fst (Φ x) = G(x) for every x ∈ E.
   (a) Derivative. Let x ∈ V. The map y ↦ (G(y), π(y − a)) has derivative v ↦ (DG(x)v, πv) at x: the first component by step 1, the second because π is continuous linear and y ↦ y − a has derivative id. Composing with the continuous linear map T, Φ has derivative DΦ(x) := T ∘ (DG(x), π) at x, i.e. DΦ(x)v = T(DG(x)v, πv). In particular fderiv ℝ Φ x = DΦ(x).
   (b) Smoothness. The map y ↦ (G(y), π(y − a)) is C¹ on V, because G is C¹ on V and y ↦ π(y − a) is affine. T is continuous linear, so Φ is C¹ on V. Since V is open, x ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ x is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
5. DΦ(a) is invertible.
   - Let v ∈ E with DΦ(a)v = 0. Since T is injective, Lv = 0 and πv = 0. So v ∈ K₀ and e(v) = π(v) = 0, hence v = 0 because e is injective.
   - So DΦ(a) : E → P is an injective linear map between spaces of the same finite dimension m + k, and therefore also surjective (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank).
   - Let Φ'ₐ : E ≃L[ℝ] P be the continuous linear equivalence whose underlying map is DΦ(a). By step 4, Φ has derivative Φ'ₐ at a. Φ is C¹ at a because V is an open neighbourhood of a.
6. The invertibility set.
   - Let 𝓘 be the set of continuous linear maps E → P that are underlying maps of continuous linear equivalences E ≃L[ℝ] P. 𝓘 is open in the space of continuous linear maps (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen; E is complete).
   - Let V′ := {x ∈ V : fderiv ℝ Φ x ∈ 𝓘}. Since x ↦ fderiv ℝ Φ x is continuous on the open set V (step 4(b)), V′ is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage).
   - Since fderiv ℝ Φ a = DΦ(a) = Φ'ₐ, we have a ∈ V′.
7. Inverse function theorem. Apply the C¹ inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) to Φ at a, with derivative Φ'ₐ and smoothness order 1 ≠ 0. It gives an open partial homeomorphism h from E to P whose underlying function is Φ and whose source S contains a. Its source S and target S′ are open. Its inverse Λ₀ := h.symm : P → E is a function on all of P and satisfies:
   - for p ∈ S′: Λ₀(p) ∈ S and Φ(Λ₀(p)) = p;
   - for x ∈ S: Φ(x) ∈ S′ and Λ₀(Φ(x)) = x;
   - Λ₀ is continuous on S′ and injective on S′.
8. Definitions.
   - V₁ := S ∩ V′. It is open, a ∈ V₁ (steps 6 and 7), and V₁ ⊆ V′ ⊆ V.
   - Ω := {p ∈ S′ : Λ₀(p) ∈ V₁}. It is open because Λ₀ is continuous on the open set S′ and V₁ is open (OpenPartialHomeomorph.isOpen_inter_preimage_symm).
   - Λ := Λ₀.
9. Λ(Ω) = V₁. If p ∈ Ω, then Λ(p) ∈ V₁ by definition. Conversely, let x ∈ V₁. Then x ∈ S, so p := Φ(x) ∈ S′ and Λ(p) = x ∈ V₁; hence p ∈ Ω and x = Λ(p). So Λ(Ω) = V₁, which is open, contains a and is contained in V.
10. Injectivity. Λ is injective on Ω, since Ω ⊆ S′ and Λ is injective on S′.
11. C¹ regularity and derivative of Λ.
   - Let p ∈ Ω and x := Λ(p) ∈ V₁. Since x ∈ V′, there is a continuous linear equivalence φₓ : E ≃L[ℝ] P whose underlying map is fderiv ℝ Φ x.
   - Since x ∈ V, Φ is differentiable at x (steps 1 and 4), so Φ has derivative φₓ at x = Λ(p). Φ is C¹ at x because V is an open neighbourhood of x.
   - Since p ∈ S′, the target of h, OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm shows that Λ is C¹ at p, and OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm shows that Λ has derivative φₓ⁻¹ at p.
   - Hence fderiv ℝ Λ p = φₓ⁻¹, the underlying map of a linear equivalence P ≃ E, which is bijective.
   - Λ is C¹ at every point of the open set Ω, so it is C¹ on Ω.
12. The first component. For p ∈ Ω ⊆ S′, Φ(Λ(p)) = p (step 7). Hence G(Λ(p)) = WithLp.fst (Φ(Λ(p))) = WithLp.fst p (step 4).
13. Conclusion. Ω is open (8). Λ is C¹ on Ω (11) and injective on Ω (10). Λ(Ω) is open, contains a and is contained in V (9). fderiv ℝ Λ p is bijective for every p ∈ Ω (11). G(Λ p) = WithLp.fst p for every p ∈ Ω (12). This is exactly the claimed statement.
proof_key_steps: Rank-nullity: K₀ := ker DG(a) has dimension k because DG(a) : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᵐ is surjective.
Choose a linear isomorphism e : K₀ ≅ ℝᵏ and a linear left inverse r of the inclusion K₀ ↪ ℝ^{m+k}. Then π := e∘r is continuous linear and π = e on K₀.
Φ(x) := toLp(G x, π(x − a)) is C¹ on V, with DΦ(x)v = toLp(DG(x)v, πv) and WithLp.fst ∘ Φ = G.
DΦ(a) is injective (kernel argument via e), hence bijective since both spaces have dimension m + k.
V′ := {x ∈ V : fderiv Φ x is a continuous linear equivalence} is open (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen and continuity of fderiv Φ on V) and contains a.
C¹ inverse function theorem at a gives a partial homeomorphism h with underlying map Φ. Set V₁ := source ∩ V′, Ω := target ∩ h.symm⁻¹(V₁) (open), Λ := h.symm.
Λ(Ω) = V₁ is open, contains a and lies in V. Λ is injective on Ω. At p ∈ Ω, Λ is C¹ with derivative DΦ(Λp)⁻¹, which is bijective (contDiffAt_symm, hasFDerivAt_symm).
G(Λ p) = WithLp.fst(Φ(Λ p)) = WithLp.fst p, because Φ(Λ p) = p on the target.

subproblems.title: Reparametrizing a Simon local representation by a C¹ diffeomorphism
subproblems.statement: Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ, n := m + k, and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ). Let M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ. That is: V and W are open; ψ is C¹ on V and injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ M; ψ is proper relative to V and W; and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Assume tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for every x ∈ V. Let Ω ⊆ P be open, and let Λ : P → ℝⁿ be C¹ on Ω and injective on Ω, with Λ(Ω) open, Λ(Ω) ⊆ V, and fderiv ℝ Λ p bijective for every p ∈ Ω. Then there is an open set O ⊆ ℝᴺ such that: (ψ ∘ Λ)(Ω) = O ∩ M; ψ ∘ Λ is C¹ on Ω and injective on Ω; and for every p ∈ Ω, the derivative fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ Λ) p is injective and tangentSpace M ((ψ ∘ Λ) p) = range(fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ Λ) p).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn (m + k) → Rn N) (Ω : Set (WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k))) (Λ : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) → Rn (m + k)), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ → (∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) → IsOpen Ω → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Λ Ω → InjOn Λ Ω → IsOpen (Λ '' Ω) → Λ '' Ω ⊆ V → (∀ p ∈ Ω, Function.Bijective (fderiv ℝ Λ p)) → ∃ O : Set (Rn N), IsOpen O ∧ (ψ ∘ Λ) '' Ω = O ∩ M ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (ψ ∘ Λ) Ω ∧ InjOn (ψ ∘ Λ) Ω ∧ (∀ p ∈ Ω, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ Λ) p)) ∧ ∀ p ∈ Ω, tangentSpace M ((ψ ∘ Λ) p) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ Λ) p).toLinearMap
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 (a), (b), (c), (d) and (f) of the parent proof. Here Λ is an arbitrary C¹ map with the stated properties; in the parent it is the inverse chart from the local submersion theorem.

Notation.
- n := m + k, P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), Ψ := ψ ∘ Λ : P → ℝᴺ, V₁ := Λ(Ω).
- Dψ(x) := fderiv ℝ ψ x and DΛ(p) := fderiv ℝ Λ p.
- (hTψ) is the hypothesis tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for all x ∈ V.

0. Unpacking the hypothesis IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ:
   - V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ are open;
   - ψ is C¹ on V and injective on V;
   - ψ(V) = W ∩ M;
   - ψ is proper relative to V and W, i.e. V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W;
   - Dψ(x) is injective for every x ∈ V.
1. Λ maps Ω into V. For p ∈ Ω, Λ(p) ∈ Λ(Ω) = V₁ ⊆ V.
2. The open set O. V₁ is open and V₁ ⊆ V. Simon 4.2 is available as SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.SubmanifoldTopology). Its proof uses the relative properness from step 0 to show that ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M. It gives an open O ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M. Hence Ψ(Ω) = ψ(Λ(Ω)) = ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M.
3. Ψ is C¹ on Ω. ψ is C¹ on V, Λ is C¹ on Ω, and Λ maps Ω into V (step 1). So Ψ = ψ ∘ Λ is C¹ on Ω (ContDiffOn.comp).
4. Ψ is injective on Ω. Let p, q ∈ Ω with ψ(Λ p) = ψ(Λ q). Then Λ p, Λ q ∈ V (step 1), so Λ p = Λ q because ψ is injective on V, and then p = q because Λ is injective on Ω.
5. Chain rule. Let p ∈ Ω.
   - Ω is open and Λ is C¹ on Ω, so Λ is differentiable at p.
   - Λ(p) ∈ V, V is open and ψ is C¹ on V, so ψ is differentiable at Λ(p).
   - By the chain rule (fderiv_comp), fderiv ℝ Ψ p = Dψ(Λ p) ∘ DΛ(p).
6. Injective derivative. Dψ(Λ p) is injective by step 0, since Λ p ∈ V. DΛ(p) is injective because it is bijective by hypothesis. So the composite fderiv ℝ Ψ p = Dψ(Λ p) ∘ DΛ(p) is injective.
7. Tangent spaces.
   - By (hTψ) at x = Λ(p) ∈ V: tangentSpace M (Ψ p) = tangentSpace M (ψ(Λ p)) = range Dψ(Λ p).
   - Since DΛ(p) is surjective: range(Dψ(Λ p) ∘ DΛ(p)) = Dψ(Λ p)(range DΛ(p)) = Dψ(Λ p)(P) = range Dψ(Λ p) (LinearMap.range_comp_of_range_eq_top).
   - By step 5 the left-hand side is range(fderiv ℝ Ψ p). Hence tangentSpace M (Ψ p) = range(fderiv ℝ Ψ p).
8. Conclusion. For this O: O is open and Ψ(Ω) = O ∩ M (2); Ψ is C¹ on Ω (3) and injective on Ω (4); and for every p ∈ Ω, fderiv ℝ Ψ p is injective (6) and tangentSpace M (Ψ p) = range(fderiv ℝ Ψ p) (7). This is exactly the claimed statement.
proof_key_steps: Λ(Ω) ⊆ V, so Λ maps Ω into the chart domain V.
Simon 4.2 (IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter) applied to the open set V₁ = Λ(Ω) ⊆ V gives an open O with (ψ∘Λ)(Ω) = ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M.
ψ∘Λ is C¹ on Ω (ContDiffOn.comp) and injective on Ω (InjOn.comp).
Chain rule: D(ψ∘Λ)(p) = Dψ(Λp) ∘ DΛ(p), which is injective as a composite of injective maps.
DΛ(p) is surjective, so range D(ψ∘Λ)(p) = range Dψ(Λp) = tangentSpace M (ψ(Λp)) by the tangent hypothesis at Λp ∈ V.
